use: a recap of something built in pieces
request: End of my water cycle lesson: a quick recap that puts the four stages back together.
intent: A teacher wants a recap at the end of a lesson that has already built each stage.
goal: The viewer can name the four stages in order and sees them as one loop.
promise: The whole loop once more, fast.
arc: Four empty places, each stage arriving quickly in order, then the whole loop lit once more.

events.text: So, the whole loop, one more time.
events.knows: This is a recap of four stages.
events.look: four places waiting in a loop

events.text: The sun heats the ocean, and water rises as vapor.
events.look: evaporation: vapor rising from the ocean

events.text: High up, it cools into clouds.
Clouds drop it as rain or snow.
And it runs back to the sea.
events.look: collection: water running to the sea

events.text: Same water, around and around, for billions of years.

holds.does: the whole loop lights stage by stage once more

measure.derived: Derived once from the request, intent and audience; thresholds not named here take the defaults in bench/lib/settings.ts. Read sizes scale with how wide the frame looks: a classroom or meeting screen from the back looks narrower than a phone at arm's length, a laptop at a desk wider. A hold listed as still is one the plan asks to wait without motion.

context.why: the end of a lesson in class

quiz.a: The sun heating the ocean, so water rises as vapor.

quiz.q: What happens to the vapor high up?
In what order did the four stages come?
quiz.a: Evaporation, condensation (clouds), precipitation (rain or snow), collection (back to the sea).

quiz.q: What did the picture do at the very end?
quiz.a: It showed the whole loop and lit each stage in order once more.

quiz.q: How many places were waiting at the start, and in what arrangement?
In the final replay, which stage lit first?
Which way does the vapor move in the first stage?
